text.p: The Florida Marlins, who failed in their efforts to sign free agent slugger Albert Belle, landed Bobby Bonilla on Friday, giving him a four-year contract and reuniting him with his old manager.
Financial terms were not disclosed, but broadcast reports put the contract in excess of $5 million per season.
The deal reunites Bonilla with Marlins manager Jim Leyland, his former skipper with the Pittsburgh Pirates.
The 33-year-old Bonilla hit .287 with 28 homers and 116 runs batted in for the Baltimore Orioles last season.
The five-time All-Star, however, slumped in the American League Championship Series against the Yankees, getting just one hit in 20 at-bats as the Orioles lost in five games.
Bonilla (corrects from Belle) played third base and outfield last season and was frequently used as a designated hitter -- an option that will not be available with the National League Marlins.
The Marlins will be the fifth major league team for Bonilla, who has also played for the Chicago White Sox and New York Mets. He is a lifetime .284 hitter with 245 homers and 965 RBI.

Belle received an offer from the Marlins worth over $8 million per season, but the former Cleveland Indians outfielder instead signed a five-year, $55 million deal with the Chicago White Sox earlier this week.

The Marlins have been aggressively pursuing free agents to aid an offence that scored just 688 runs last season, the third lowest total in the National League. They outbid the Chicago Cubs and San Francisco Giants for Bonilla.
With slugger Gary Sheffield in right field, Devon White in centre and Jeff Conine in left, Bonilla seems most likely to be used at third base.
